items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: Sonny Henry? Yeah, he worked with him all the time, too.

ctx.x: What about trombone? Did you have a steady trombone player?
Well, no. Henry, most all of them all has played with us, you know, off and on like that, you know. Sonny Henry? Yeah, he worked with him all the time, too.
Sonny or Chicken Henry? Which one? Sonny.

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I like Henry's playing, Sonny Henry.

ctx.x: No, no, no, Joe died, no. In other words he's claiming tommene poison. Well I forgot of him, wasn't he? Yeah.
Did he die after his brother Henry?
Oh he died after Henry, yeah, from tommene poison, food, food poison.

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Let's see. I think Sonny Henry, I think he played trombone a lot.

ctx.x: Trying to think of who'd be playing trombone with that band.

Will he playin' drum go? Let me see. Jim Crow. Jim Crow. Let me see what Jim Crow. No, no. Jim Crow. I don't know. I just remember now. Was it Sonny Henry with the. No, this fellow was playing the bass with Sadie, Chinese, Buddy PT. But now. Did he have a banjo player? Johnny, yeah. We didn't see there. No, Johnny. Yeah, that's with Johnny, Johnny, David. You were in that band? No, Johnny was on the boat. Yeah, but Johnny, wait, I'm trying to get that together now. No, Johnny wasn't with them, no.

Seems to me he was probably with Sam Morgan then. I'm trying to remember now. About that time. He and Jim Crow would have been playing with Sam Morgan. Yeah. And uh, did you ever know George Washington?
